title: Sparse-tiling KV residency: tile-based eviction, oversubscription budget and async host fallback
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Background: As request concurrency increases across mixed-length chat workloads, our monolithic KV slab tends to create hotspots and long tail OOMs when a small fraction of prompts cause large attention state growth. Goal: implement a sparse tile-based residency model for the KV cache that lets us evict and migrate at tile granularity (e.g., 64-token tiles), enforce an oversubscription budget per-GPU, and provide an async host fallback path so sockets can continue serving with degraded latency when device memory is exhausted. This ticket covers the low-level implementation details, safety invariants, and telemetry we need to ship an initial safe canary.
acceptance_criteria: Tile-based residency map implemented (tile size configurable, default 64 tokens)
Eviction policy supports soft watermarks and progressive prefetching when below low watermark
Per-GPU oversubscription budget accepted by scheduler and exposed in runtime config
Async host-fallback path implemented: read-only KV misses get served from host pages with measurable latency fallback
End-to-end tests demonstrating no hard OOMs under synthetic oversubscription workloads (2x memory pressure) and graceful latency degradation
Telemetry: tile-level residency, migration latency histogram, eviction counts, oversubscription fill gauge emitted to console and traces
implementation_notes: Introduce ResidencyMap: compact bitmap per-model-per-device where each bit represents a tile residency (on-device / on-host / migrating)
Device-backed Slabs remain but are split logically into fixed tile slots; allocation returns (slab_id, tile_index)
Soft watermarks: HIGH (80%) triggers aggressive batching-friendly eviction; LOW (60%) starts proactive prefetch from host for hot tiles
Eviction policy: LRU at tile granularity with age buckets to avoid thrashing for long-lived contexts
Oversubscription budget: scheduler can create 'staging allocations' that are immediately pinned to host until device space freed; budget is global per-GPU and adjustable via API
Async host fallback: reads that hit on-host tiles are served from pinned host buffers via GPU DMA path where possible; fallback falls back to CPU memcpy if DMA slots saturated
Consistency: migration must be lock-free for readers. Use sequence counters on ResidencyMap entries to detect in-flight migrations and retry reads (single retry)
Batching integration: continuous batcher must be KV-aware and prefer grouping requests with overlapping tile sets to avoid redundant device migrations
Safety: fail-open boolean flag to prevent eviction if explicit customer pinning is set for a model (dedicated/private customers can opt-out)
Memory accounting: report device-resident tokens vs host-resident tokens for cost and SLO reporting
benchmarks_and_results: Local microbench: synthetic chat workload (uniform 1-4k seq len) with 4 concurrent streams: tile-based eviction reduced device migration count by ~48% vs baseline slab eviction

Oversubscription stress: when pushing to 2.2x nominal memory, system had zero hard OOMs and 95th pct latency increased by 1.9x with host-fallback enabled; without host-fallback hard OOMs triggered in 75% runs
Batcher synergy test: grouping by overlapping tiles improved end-to-end throughput 1.3x for long-context workloads
Telemetry: migration latency p50=6ms, p95=28ms for device->host migrations under load (first canary results)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Increased CPU overhead for host-backed reads — we mitigate with DMA and batching but some tail cost remains
Tile granularity choice is workload-dependent; too-small tiles increase metadata and migration churn, too-large reduce flexibility — chosen 64-token default is a conservative compromise
Lock-free migration complexity: sequence counters reduce stalls but add subtle retry semantics; must be audited carefully
Customer UX: dedicated customers who expect strict device residency may see degraded throughput when oversubscription is used — provide explicit opt-out flag
plan: Phase 1 (Spike & API): implement ResidencyMap, tile allocator, and telemetry hooks. Validate with unit tests. (owner: Liam)
Phase 2 (Runtime integration): integrate eviction/migration paths, oversubscription budget enforcement, and host-fallback DMA. Add canary config. (owner: Priya + runtime)
Phase 3 (Canary): rollout to 5% of traffic on canary fleet with intensive synthetic tests and customer workload replay
Phase 4 (Iterate): tweak tile size heuristics, add workload-driven auto-tuner for oversubscription budget, and document SLO impacts
